title: Benchmark result
description: Schema for one benchmark run contributed under benchmarks/{type}/{model}/results/<tier-or-unranked>/<result_id>.json (one subfolder per pinned VRAM tier plus unranked; types without tiers put files directly in results/). The file name must equal <result_id>.json. Results are append-only: never edit a merged file, add a new one with 'supersedes' instead.

result_id.description: Unique id, also the file name without extension. Format: <date>-<contributor>-<model_family>[-tag]-<suffix>, where <suffix> is 6 random lowercase hex characters (e.g. a1b2c3) so nobody has to check for collisions by hand. Example: 2026-08-15-alice-qwen3.8-27b-a1b2c3.

benchmark_type.description: Must equal the top-level folder name under benchmarks/ (e.g. inference-speed).

model_family.description: Canonical base model id, must equal the folder name under benchmarks/{type}/ (e.g. qwen3.8-27b). Quantization is NOT part of the folder.

contributor.description: GitHub username of the person who ran the test.

date.description: Date the run was executed, YYYY-MM-DD.

name.description: Tool used to run the benchmark, e.g. llama-bench.

version.description: Exact tool/build version or tag, e.g. b6500 for a llama.cpp build.

protocol_version.description: Version of the PROTOCOL.md followed for this benchmark type, e.g. 1.0.

quantization.description: Quantization of the tested file, e.g. UD-Q4_K_XL.

repo_id.description: Where the model file came from, e.g. unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF on Hugging Face.

file.description: Exact model file used, e.g. Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf. Recommended for every run.

cpu.description: CPU model (optional - not used for ranking), e.g. AMD Ryzen 9 7950X.

gpu.description: GPU type (include VRAM) - the one required hardware fact, e.g. NVIDIA RTX 3090 (24 GB). null for CPU-only runs.

ram_gb.description: System RAM in GiB/GB (optional - not used for ranking).

vram_gb.description: GPU VRAM in GB, recorded as the card's marketed class (a '32 GB' card that reports 31.9 counts as 32; unified memory on systems like the NVIDIA DGX Spark counts too; multi-GPU rigs: combined total). It decides which pinned tier this result can rank in (low-end = 16 / med-end = 24 / high-end = 32 / time-traveler > 32).

os.description: Operating system and version, e.g. Windows 11 / Ubuntu 24.04.

settings.description: Runtime settings relevant to comparability. Which keys are REQUIRED per benchmark type is defined by config/benchmark_types.json (inference-speed v1.0 requires: n_gpu_layers, context_length, kv_cache_quant, mtp_enabled; ranked rows must also reproduce their VRAM tier's pinned recipe, e.g. spec_draft_n_max + flash_attn for qwen3.8-27b). Record the values you ACTUALLY ran. `prompt_tokens` (nominal prompt size of the prompt preset in tokens) is recommended for inference-speed runs.

metrics.description: Numeric metrics named by the PROTOCOL.md of the benchmark type. Only numbers, so results stay comparable and sortable.

comment.description: Short note about this run (conditions, caveats, why it differs). Shown in the Comment column of LEADERBOARD.md. Keep it short; longer text belongs in 'notes'.

raw_output_file.description: Sibling file (<result_id>.raw.txt) containing the verbatim tool output, for auditability. Recommended for every result.

supersedes.description: result_id of a previous (erroneous) run this one replaces (same format: lowercase segments plus the 6-char random suffix). The old file stays in the repo untouched and is excluded from leaderboards.

notes.description: Optional longer free text: ambient conditions, why this supersedes an earlier entry. Not shown as a leaderboard column.
